texts: bad: "near the third cliff-spire" is stored as the finding's Location, the in/at/on head — it says the find happened AT the spire rather than near it, so the proximity is distorted, not merely coarsened. Move the proximity onto the feather as its own position clause, where the surface preposition survives: "On day 440 of Year 2, Tessa Brae found a large sky-cat feather. The feather lay near the third cliff-spire." The in-world date does carry as Day 440 plus Year 2, but nothing marks it as a day-of-year rather than a day-of-month — a limitation no rewording of yours can fix.
good. the past-wrapped "long" and a separate "unusually" degree atom both land, on the same feather symbol introduced in the first sentence.
good. the add event carries Tessa Brae as agent, the feather as theme and the feather store as its goal, with feather_store linked to store.

bad: "might belong to" puts the possessed thing in subject position, a shape the instruction set has no route for — the parse forced it into the possession roles reserved for own/have/lack, and the licensed repair (a plain "to" oblique on the belonging) would drop the feather-to-cat link altogether, so "whose feather is it?" would find nothing. Put the possessor in the subject: "Tessa Brae reported to the Council that a new sky-cat might own the feather." If you mean origin rather than ownership, "…that the feather might have come from a new sky-cat" is the other cleanly-parsing option. Separately, the coined kind sky_cat is left with no link to cat, which nothing in your wording controls.

good. the whole taking is recorded as a strength-0 denial with the Council as its agent; only the quantifier word "no" itself goes unrecorded, and it costs nothing here because the denial already says it.
